title: 1988–89 National Hurling League
text:
{{Short description|58th season of the National Hurling League}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 1988–89 National Hurling League |image = |dates = 30 October 1988 – 30 April 1989 |teams = |team1 = Galway |captain1 = [[Conor Hayes]] |manager1 = [[Cyril Farrell]] |titles = 5th |team2 = Tipperary |captain2 = [[Pat McGrath (Tipperary hurler)|Pat McGrath]] |manager2 = [[Michael Keating (hurler)|Michael "Babs" Keating]] |two = |three = |four = |previous = [[1987–88 National Hurling League|1987–88]] |next = [[1989–90 National Hurling League|1989–90]] }} The '''1988–89 National Hurling League''', known for sponsorship reasons as the '''[[Royal Liver Assurance|Royal Liver]] National Hurling League''', was the 58th season of the [[National Hurling League]] (NHL), an annual [[hurling]] competition for the [[GAA county teams]].{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|title=National Hurling League Results 1925-2009|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=18 April 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100805063526/http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|archive-date=2010-08-05|url-status=dead}}{{cite book |last= Smith|first=Raymond |date=1999 |title=Complete Handbook of Gaelic Games |location=Dublin, Ireland |page=208 |isbn=0950175870}} It was won by {{GG|Galway|hurling}}. This season was notable as the first to hold both semi-finals and the final at [[Croke Park]], giving the League additional prestige.{{Cite web|url=https://deiseach.wordpress.com/national-hurling-league-19889/|title=National Hurling League 1988/9|date=15 January 2011}} ==Division 1== {{Infobox football league season |competition=[[National Hurling League|National Hurling League Division 1]] |season=1988-89 |winners=[[Galway GAA|Galway]]
5th National League title
Captain: [[Conor Hayes]]
Manager: [[Cyril Farrell]] |relegated=[[Offaly GAA|Offaly]]
[[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] |continentalcup1= |continentalcup1 qualifiers= |continentalcup2= |continentalcup2 qualifiers= |league topscorer=[[File: Colours of Kilkenny.svg|border|20px]] [[Adrian Ronan]] (2-47) |best goalkeeper= |biggest home win= |biggest away win= |highest scoring= |matches= 35 |total goals= |longest wins= |longest unbeaten= |longest winless= |longest losses= |highest attendance= |lowest attendance= |attendance= |average attendance= |prevseason=[[1987-88 National Hurling League|1987-88]] |nextseason=[[1989-90 National Hurling League|1989-90]] |updated= }} [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] came into the season as defending champions of the [[1987–88 National Hurling League|1987-88 season]]. [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]] and [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] entered Division 1 as the two promoted teams. On 30 April 1989, [[Galway GAA|Galway]] won the title after a 2-16 to 4-8 win over Tipperary. It was their first league title since 1987 and their fifth National League title overall.{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|title=National Hurling League Results 1925-2009|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=18 April 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100805063526/http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|archive-date=2010-08-05|url-status=dead}} [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] were the first team to be relegated after losing all of but one of their group stage games, while Offaly suffered the same fate after losing a series of play-off games with Antrim and [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]].
